entry.title: Transactions,Deadlocks and Log Based Recovery
entry.summary:
💡 Objective: We’ll use a simple Accounts table to demonstrate these core database concept INSERT INTO Accounts VALUES
A transaction is a group of SQL operations executed as a single logical unit. Example: Transfer ₹500 from Alice → Bob, then rollback. -- Debit Alice -- Credit Bob -- Rollback before committing -- Check balances
A deadlock occurs when two transactions hold locks that the other needs. 🧩 Session 1 -- Lock Alice’s account -- Try to update Bob’s balance (will wait if Session 2 has locked Bob)
-- Lock Bob’s account -- Try to update Alice’s balance (will wait if Session 1 has locked Alice) Example Error (MySQL): ERROR 1213 (40001): Deadlock found when trying to get lock; try restarting transaction 💬 Explanation:
🧾 Step 4: Log-Based Recovery Modern databases maintain logs to record every transaction’s activity. Example: Observe undo logging via rollback -- Update Charlie’s balance -- Rollback -- Verify balance restored 💬 Explanation: The database writes the undo log entry when you start the transaction. When rollback is issued, the DB uses that log to restore previous values
